Responsible Use of Predictive Models in Teaching

Predictive systems can help teachers identify where a class needs more support, but useful adoption depends on transparent limits and careful interpretation rather than mechanical ranking.

Argument

A model should be treated as an additional signal. The instructor still decides which intervention is pedagogically appropriate, especially when the available data captures only a partial view of student effort.

Risk score: p(y=1 \mid x)=\sigma(w^\top x)

Conclusion

The best classroom workflow combines automation with review, explanation, and a clear route for students to contest or contextualize a prediction.
